sections.h2: Five-year consumer inflation: China 3.5%, Brazil 35.7%, a tenfold gap

chart.title: Brazil's consumer prices rose ten times as much as China's in five years
chart.sub: Cumulative consumer price rise, 2020 to 2025, %. Argentina (1,811.3%) omitted for scale.

sections.means: On one harmonised source, Brazil's five-year consumer rise was ten times China's, so the spread is real.

sections.h2: Producer prices re-accelerated across five economies in the first half of 2026

chart.title: US producer prices were up 12.3% in May, the highest of five economies
chart.sub: Year-on-year %, May 2026. China is not shown as monthly releases are not archived.
chart.source: Official national producer price series, retrieved 8 August 2026.

sections.means: US producer prices rose from +2.4% in January to +12.3% in May, and the other four economies accelerated too.
sections.todo: Watch the official July and August producer prints to see whether the 2026 spike was short-lived.

sections.h2: Producer prices: Brazil's four-year rise is the largest, China's the smallest

chart.title: Brazil's producer prices rose 47.9% over four years, China's 4.9%
chart.sub: Cumulative producer price rise over the four years to 2024, %. Harmonised series.
chart.source: World Bank, Global Database of Inflation; author's calculation.

sections.means: Brazil's producer prices rose early and high in 2020 and 2021 as its currency fell, so the index partly measures the exchange rate.
